title: Best Golf Shoes UK
short: Twelve golf shoes tested over multiple rounds and weather conditions, spiked and spikeless, compared on comfort, grip, stability and waterproofing.
intro: A golf shoe's real test is how it holds up over many rounds in changing weather, not a short indoor trial. This guide compares shoes tested by Golf Monthly, where every pair was personally worn by a member of the team over extended periods. The category is overseen by footwear expert Dan Parker, who checks manufacturers' claims such as waterproofing and tests across different ground conditions, stances, lies and walking demands. All twelve shoes are covered here, split between spiked and spikeless.

products.name: Drive Pro Clone SL
products.best_for: Golfers who want comfort, stability and versatility on and off the course
products.key_spec: Spikeless, adaptive auxetic upper, rubber nubs with TPU outsole, waterproof, sizes 6-14
products.summary: Golf Monthly's top pick, called one of the best golf shoes their tester has ever worn. The adaptive upper gives a snug, pinch-free fit for different foot shapes, and the outsole blends rubber nubs with TPU for ground penetration and lateral stability, with a refined, premium look. The one drawback is that it isn't as breathable as some other spikeless golf shoes in very high temperatures.
pros: Adaptive fit offers both comfort and strong stability
Class-leading outsole with ground penetration and lateral stability
Premium looks and feel with on-course versatility
cons: Not as breathable as some other spikeless golf shoes
products.search: Under Armour Drive Pro Clone SL golf shoe

products.name: Drive Pro Clone (spiked)
products.best_for: Golfers who want tour-level stability and traction in a spiked shoe
products.key_spec: Spiked, auxetic adaptive upper, S3 support system, waterproof, sizes 6-14
products.summary: Narrowly missing the overall top pick, this takes the 'Best Spiked' title for its tour-level stability and comfort. The upper adapts to the contours of any foot, combining the flexibility of knit shoes with locked-in stability, and the S3 support system gives industry-leading traction, though underfoot cushioning is firmer than the softest shoes and it's slightly less breathable.
pros: Upper moulds to create an adaptive fit for any foot shape
cons: Not as breathable as other shoes
products.search: Under Armour Drive Pro Clone spiked golf shoe

products.name: Biom C5
products.best_for: Golfers who want premium comfort, breathability and durability
products.key_spec: Gore-Tex Surround waterproofing, improved heel lockdown, premium leather, sizes 5-13
products.summary: Golf Monthly found these fitted like a glove, with a noticeably improved heel lockdown over the C4 for swinging aggressively, great breathability and premium materials that give exceptional walking comfort. Gore-Tex Surround gives total waterproofing without sacrificing breathability, though the price is hefty and the outsole isn't class-leading.
pros: More locked-in heel than the previous model

products.name: S2G SL
products.best_for: Golfers who want a budget-friendly shoe that also works away from the course
products.key_spec: Spikeless crossover shoe, Lightstrike midsole, wider fit than most adidas golf shoes, sizes 6.5-14.5
products.summary: Golf Monthly's best-value pick, a running-shoe-inspired crossover that looks as natural at the pub as on the links. It fits true to size with a wider fit than most adidas golf shoes, making it one of the best for wide feet, with a Lightstrike midsole and a price that falls in the best budget category, though it isn't as breathable as some.

products.name: Quantum
products.best_for: Golfers who walk most rounds and play mainly in summer conditions
products.key_spec: Ortholite Impression FitBed, SofFoam heel, waterproof, BOA option, sizes 6-14
products.summary: Arguably the most comfortable golf shoe of the year, with class-leading comfort underfoot from a FitBed that gives instant step-in comfort and gradually moulds to your foot, plus a soft, premium upper. That focus on comfort means it doesn't offer quite the same stability and traction as the top spiked shoes, and it isn't the best-looking shoe in the guide.
pros: Versatile outsole can be worn on and off the course
cons: Neither here nor there from a style perspective
Less stability and traction than the top spiked shoes

products.name: 997 SL
products.best_for: Golfers who want a lifestyle-runner look for warm-weather rounds and range trips
products.key_spec: Spikeless, Ndurance rubber outsole, Abzorb midsole, CUSH+ insole, sizes 7-12.5
products.summary: Golf Monthly found a comfortable, lightweight walking shoe with plush padding around the heel and ankle and a surprising amount of grip from strategically placed rubber nubs, in a style that looks as good on the high street as on the course. Some golfers may notice a lack of targeted support under the ball of the foot, suede detailing is best kept away from mud, and Golf Monthly recommends ordering a half size larger.
pros: Minimalist style will appeal to most
Great grip in a range of conditions
Padding around the ankle provides great comfort
cons: More support around the ball of the foot would be welcomed
Suede detailing is best kept away from muddy conditions

products.name: G.112 (2026)
products.best_for: Golfers who want an incredibly light spikeless summer shoe with a massaging insole
products.key_spec: Spikeless, nubbed massaging insole, water repellent, sizes 6-14
products.summary: Golf Monthly found these incredibly lightweight yet locked in tightly for the swing, with enough give to avoid rubbing or blisters. The star is G/FORE's signature nubbed, massaging insole, which relieves fatigue over 18 holes, and the low-profile outsole gives dependable traction on dry and damp turf, though testers expected higher-end materials for the price.
pros: One of the best insoles on modern golf shoes
cons: Would expect higher-end materials for the price point

products.name: Premiere Series Packard (2026)
products.best_for: Golfers who want a traditional, brogue-style premium leather shoe
products.key_spec: Premium leather with nubuck and bison-textured panel, waterproof, multi-directional traction, sizes 6-14
products.summary: One of, if not the fanciest pair of golf shoes money can buy, with a nubuck leather centre panel and refined toe accents. It's lighter than previous versions with added heel and tongue comfort, a stable and secure platform for the swing, and strong multi-directional traction in wet conditions, though there are softer underfoot shoes on the market.
pros: Stunning looks and attention to detail
Added comfort in the heel and tongue
cons: There are softer underfoot shoes on the market
products.search: FootJoy Premiere Series Packard 2026 golf shoe

products.name: Victory Tour 4
products.best_for: Golfers who want a high-performance tour shoe with a rock-solid base
products.key_spec: Spiked, Dynamic Fit lockdown, Cushlon midsole, waterproof, sizes 6-14
products.summary: Worn by Rory McIlroy on the PGA Tour, these deliver a slightly firmer feel with plenty of comfort and stability. Golf Monthly found the Dynamic Fit system gives extra lockdown, the Cushlon midsole gives plush walking comfort without losing a solid base, and the spiked traction was a highlight, with no slipping at maximum swing speed, though it is perhaps a step back aesthetically.
pros: Comfort a real focus from the brand
products.search: Nike Air Zoom Victory Tour 4 golf shoe

products.name: Eighty Seven SC
products.best_for: Golfers who prioritise grip and a refined look
products.key_spec: Full-length carbon fibre propulsion plate, seven SoftSpikes Tour Flex Pro spikes, waterproof, sizes 7-12
products.summary: Golf Monthly found very little to fault in an outstanding all-round shoe, worn on tour by players such as Jason Day and Justin Rose. Its grip can go toe-to-toe with any shoe available, driven by a carbon fibre propulsion plate and seven SoftSpikes, with excellent underfoot cushioning and a locked-in tour feel, though the malleable upper material needs to be looked after closely.
cons: Malleable upper material needs to be looked after closely
products.search: Payntr Eighty Seven SC golf shoe

products.name: Pro/SL (2026)
products.best_for: Golfers who want spiked-shoe grip from a spikeless design
products.key_spec: Spikeless, new Z-Tec synthetic upper, class-leading outsole, very lightweight, sizes 7-15
products.summary: The iconic Pro/SL gets its biggest overhaul since 2016, swapping luxury leather for a modern synthetic upper. Golf Monthly found an exceptional spikeless outsole with elite traction even in wet and slippery conditions, good support through the swing and a very light design, though the new look will divide opinion and the forefoot cushioning is very firm.

products.name: Go Golf Blade Tour Slip-In
products.best_for: Golfers who want easy hands-free entry and out-of-the-box comfort
products.key_spec: Slip-In technology with rigid rear framework, Heel Pillow, waterproof, sizes 7-12
products.summary: Golf Monthly found an impressive all-rounder marrying Skechers' out-of-the-box comfort with strong on-course performance, with hands-free Slip-In technology and an internal Heel Pillow that locks the foot in without rubbing or blisters. It has a more premium upper than previous models and is lightweight, but it's stiffer underfoot than earlier Skechers and cluttered with too much branding.
pros: More premium upper material than previous models
cons: Stiffer underfoot than previous Skechers models
Too much writing on the shoe
products.search: Skechers Go Golf Blade Tour Slip-In golf shoe

guide.a: Spiked shoes, like the Under Armour Drive Pro Clone, Nike Victory Tour 4 and Payntr here, generally give the most traction and stability for aggressive swings and wet conditions. Spikeless shoes, like the Under Armour Clone SL, adidas S2G SL and FootJoy Pro/SL, are lighter, more comfortable for walking and often wear well off the course, and the best now grip almost as well as spiked shoes.

Very important in the UK, but not all shoes are equal. Golf Monthly checks manufacturers' waterproof claims in testing, and the Ecco Biom C5 here is rated 100% waterproof with Gore-Tex Surround, while others such as the G/FORE G.112 are only water repellent. Prioritising comfort alone can mean compromising on waterproof protection.

guide.q: Which golf shoe is best for wide feet?
guide.a: Golf Monthly named the Ecco Biom C5 best for wide feet, and found the adidas S2G SL a much wider fit than most other adidas golf shoes, true to size and one of the best for wide feet. The Under Armour Clone shoes also adapt to different foot shapes through their stretchy upper.

guide.q: Can I wear golf shoes off the course?
guide.a: Some crossover styles are designed for it. The adidas S2G SL, New Balance 997 SL and FootJoy Quantum here look natural away from the course, in line with a growing leniency in golf dress codes, though suede or knit uppers are best kept away from mud, and the most traditional shoes, like the FootJoy Packard, are more course-specific.
